title: Write and send an email
summary: Open a new message, pick a recipient from the suggestions, add a subject and text, then send it yourself.

steps.say: Click the Compose button at the top left of Gmail.

check.prompt: Is a New Message window open in Gmail?

hints: Compose has a pencil icon and sits above Inbox.
With keyboard shortcuts on, the letter c opens it too.
steps.why: Every new email starts in the compose window.

steps.say: Type the first letters of a name in the To box, then click the right person in the list.
hints: Check the email address under the name before you pick it.
Send it to yourself if you only want to practise.
steps.why: Picking from the list avoids typos in the address.

steps.say: Click Subject and type a few words about what the email is for.
hints: A short subject like Lunch on Friday works well.
steps.why: The subject is what people see first in their inbox.

steps.say: Click the big empty area below and write your message.
hints: Start with a greeting, then say what you need, then sign with your name.
steps.why: A clear message gets a faster answer.

steps.say: Read it once more, then click Send at the bottom of the window.

check.prompt: Has the compose window closed, with a Message sent notice at the bottom left?

hints: Click Undo in the notice right away if you change your mind.
steps.why: You stay in charge of sending; Lumen only writes drafts.
